data.title: Unconstrained Script Execution on Workstations
data.summary:
Standard users could execute arbitrary PowerShell, including downloaded and in-memory
content, with no application control, constrained language mode or script block logging
in place.
data.description:
PowerShell is present on every Windows host, is trusted, and provides full access to the
platform, which makes it the default execution route after initial access. Nothing has to
be dropped to disk and nothing unsigned has to run.

The three controls that matter are rarely all present. Constrained language mode removes
most offensive tooling's ability to function; application control restricts which scripts
may run at all; script block logging records what was executed even when it never touched
disk. In this environment none was enforced, so execution was both unrestricted and
unrecorded.

Execution policy is not a security control and should not be counted as one — it is
bypassed by a flag.
data.recommendation:
* Enforce constrained language mode for standard users through application control policy.
* Enable script block and module logging, and forward the resulting events centrally.
* Apply application control so only approved scripts execute, starting in audit mode to
  establish the baseline.
* Remove or restrict legacy script hosts, which are commonly used to sidestep PowerShell
  controls entirely.
data.short_recommendation: Enforce constrained language mode and enable script block logging.
